english.title: Provide later years provision for child under eight without being registered
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) without reasonable excuse provided later years provision for a child who had not attained the age of eight

(A)_[on premises which were not domestic premises, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PREMISES..), without being registered in Part A of the general childcare register]_
(B)_[on domestic premises, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PREMISES..), which would have been later years childminding but for section 96(9) of the Childcare Act 2006, without being registered in Part A of the general childcare register or with a later years childminder agency]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 53(5) and (6) of the Childcare Act 2006.
english.pointstoprove:

english.notes:
(i) Section 53(2) of the Childcare Act 2006 provides certain exceptions to the requirement to be registered concerning schools.
(ii) Other exceptions may be provided by order by the Secretary of State, Section 53(3) of the Act.
(iii) This offence no longer applies after the 31st October 2024 due to changes made by the Levelling-up and Regeneration Act 2023. For the offence applying after this date, see H101870.

other.penalty:
Summary: a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecution:
Six months from the date on which evidence sufficient in the opinion of the prosecutor to warrant the proceedings comes to his knowledge, but no more than three years after the commission of the offence.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
